system.name: Latent Policy Barrier (LPB)
system.one_liner: Robust visuomotor imitation policy that treats the latent expert distribution as a barrier and uses a learned dynamics model at inference to steer rollouts back inside it.

content.variant_note: prior interactive correction versus dynamics-guided correction, both drawn as trajectories over tinted distribution blobs with a shared legend
content.argues: Instead of widening the training data with human corrections that may be suboptimal, keep the expert distribution as a barrier and steer rollouts back to it with a learned dynamics model, without extra human input.
content.subject: Two toy rollouts from start to a star goal in a latent state space, over expert, expanded and rollout distributions, with and without human correction.

lessons.what_to_learn: Contrast an old and a new correction strategy on one identical toy task: same start, goal and expert band in two tinted panels, with the baseline's failures marked by verdict words and the new method shown as one detect-and-steer hop (coloured dot, arrow, dot).
lessons.suits: Robustness or safety methods in robotics and imitation learning that can be explained as trajectories relative to a distribution or safe set.

evidence: prior DAggerlike methods (Left) expand the training distribution via human-in-the-loop corrections
our Latent Policy Barrier treats the expert distribution ( ) as an implicit barrier
our key insight is to explicitly decouple these conflicting objectives (Figure 1 right)

summary: Latent Policy Barrier (LPB) makes behaviour-cloned visuomotor policies robust to covariate shift by keeping rollouts inside the latent distribution of expert demonstrations. Figure 1 contrasts two ways of handling drift in one visual grammar. Left, interactive correction: a human operator (silhouette and game controller) takes over at red dots, the pink training distribution grows, and some paths end suboptimal or in failure. Right, dynamics-guided correction: the expert band is outlined as a barrier inside the blue rollout distribution, a small latent-dynamics graph (z, a, z') detects a deviation (blue dot) and steers back (blue arrow) to an orange in-distribution state on the way to the red star goal. A shared legend below keys the colours.
summary_zh: 潜在策略屏障（LPB）让视觉运动策略保持在专家分布内。图1并排对比：左为人工交互纠正，扩大分布但仍可能次优或失败；右为动力学引导纠正，以橙色虚线专家分布作屏障，检测偏离并拉回。下方图例统一配色。
